thread:
maria_support: @aj_dev @jorge_sre — escalated from enterprise customer org_8765. They started seeing a lot of 504s from /v1/rerank this morning around 09:12 PT. p95 latency jumped to ~3200ms (was ~350ms) and many requests are hitting gateway timeouts. They say retries made things worse and some requests returned 502s after retrying. sample request_id: r-0a1b2c3d. Posting a sanitized example and some logs below. Can you triage? :eyes:

aj_dev: thanks — can you paste the exact payload and approximate QPS they were sending? Also which model variant are they pinning for rerank? Rerank costs scale with candidates x sequence length; large candidate lists can blow up p95.

maria_support: customer says bursts up to 200 qps with candidate lists up to 200. Model: ranker-v2 (redwood/rerank-v2). Example payload they sent:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "query": "best article about model serving",
    "candidates": ["cand_1","cand_2", ..., "cand_150"],
    "top_k": 5
  }'
```

maria_support: logs (sanitized) — repeated pattern: upstream timeout then 502s:
```
[2026-01-22T16:12:09Z] request_id=r-0a1b2c3d path=/v1/rerank status=504 upstream_time=60.001s backend=rerank-01
[2026-01-22T16:12:10Z] request_id=r-0a1b2c3d path=/v1/rerank status=502 error="upstream response error: connection reset"
[2026-01-22T16:12:10Z] request_id=r-0a1b2c3e path=/v1/rerank status=500 error="scoring timeout"
```

jorge_sre: I'm seeing matching spikes on the LB metrics — upstream 503 and 504 counts increase at the same time as request bursts. Envoy shows: 
```
cluster.rerank_upstream.upstream_cx_tx_bytes_total spike; envoy upstream_request_timeout
```
This looks like the rerank worker processes are getting overwhelmed and closing connections. Could be O(N) scoring when candidate lists are large.

aj_dev: agree — rerank-v2 does cross-attention scoring which is O(num_candidates * seq_len). At 150–200 candidates per request under 200 qps bursts, compute / memory pressure will spike. Two immediate checks:
1) Are we batching these requests server-side? If the batching window is too large, it can amplify latency under bursts.
2) Do we have a hard cap on candidates per request? I think the public API should enforce a max_candidates=100 but maybe our config drifted.

maria_support: customer insists they only started hitting errors after last Thursday's traffic increase. They can repro by sending parallel requests; they ran a local test and saw p95 go to several seconds. They've asked for a mitigation asap.

aj_dev: short repro script (quick sanity check) — reduce clients and candidates and see if errors disappear. Example (python):
```python
import requests, concurrent.futures
URL = "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank"
PAYLOAD = {"query":"x","candidates":[f"c{i}" for i in range(120)],"top_k":5}
HEADERS = {"Authorization":"Bearer sk_test_xxx"}

def call():
    r = requests.post(URL, json=PAYLOAD, headers=HEADERS, timeout=10)
    return r.status_code, r.text[:200]

with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(50) as ex:
    futures = [ex.submit(call) for _ in range(200)]
    print([f.result()[0] for f in concurrent.futures.as_completed(futures)][:10])
```

jorge_sre: I'm going to throttle the customer's traffic at the gateway and add a temporary rule to return 429 when candidate count > 120, to buy time. @ops_oncall can you push that? We'll also flip off automatic client retries from the gateway for the rerank route so we don't amplify bursts.

ops_oncall: on it. Pushing quick envoy rate-limit: set local_rate_limit for route /v1/rerank to 120r/s per org and inject response header Retry-After. Applying now — will monitor for error rate drop.

aj_dev: parallel run of debugging: I'm spinning up a dedicated canary pool with quantized model variant and lower batch window to see if we can keep tail latency down. Also adding server-side guard to reject >128 candidates with 400 + helpful message. That should avoid extreme O(N) cases.

maria_support: customer asked whether billing could be affected by retries (they were billed for multiple attempts). We should confirm how retries are logged and whether we can issue a credit if gateway retries contributed.

jorge_sre: we'll correlate request_ids and billing logs. If gateway retries were automatic, they shouldn't have been billed twice but we'll validate. I'm opening a billing ticket.

rerank-bot: incident created: INC-20260122-1135 (Rerank p95 spike under load). Assigned to eng-runtime and SRE.

aj_dev: root-cause hypothesis: no candidate-length enforcement + an increased batch window in the scoring service causing larger aggregate compute per batch leads to worker starvation and connection resets. Fix path: enforce max_candidates at API gateway, reduce batch window on rerank workers, add early-exit scoring (stop after top_k margin threshold), and improve autoscaling for rerank pool.

maria_support: next actions for today:
- SRE: rate-limit rule live (ops_oncall) — monitor 15m.
- Eng-runtime (aj_dev): push candidate limit + canary config.
- Billing: reconcile potential duplicate charges for org_8765.
- Support: ask customer to try truncated candidate list (<=50) and report success, share temporary workaround.

ops_oncall: rate-limit applied, initial telemetry shows error-rate dropping from 18% -> 6% in the affected window. Keeping rule for 2 hours while eng deploys fix.

maria_support: Thanks everyone. I'll message the customer with the temporary workaround and update the ticket. If eng needs the sample payloads or request traces, ping me and I'll send redacted logs. :white_check_mark:

aj_dev: I'll follow up with a PR for the candidate limit and a short-term batch-window tweak. Will post PR and canary link here.

jorge_sre: I'll keep monitoring LB and backend health. If p95 doesn't improve after the canary, we'll consider temporarily diverting rerank traffic to dedicated capacity.

maria_support: closing the loop here — will update once billing reconciliation and PR are done. Thanks all!
